newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Kabila fails to show, prevents Zaire talks Friday.
newsitem.headline: Kabila fails to show, prevents Zaire talks Friday.

text.p: Zaire's rebel leader Laurent Kabila failed to turn up for talks at sea on Friday with ailing President Mobutu Sese Seko and South Africa's Nelson Mandela, preventing the meeting going ahead, officials said.

One South African official told reporters on the converted icebreaker SAS Outeniqua, the talks venue in international waters of the coast of West Africa, that the meeting would not take place on Friday as planned.
It was unclear whether Outeniqua, a South African naval ship, would stay at sea or return to port.
The official said that Mandela's deputy Thabo Mbeki was coming to the ship to explain Kabila's change of heart and that things would become clearer once he had briefed the South African president.

An official source in Angola's capital Luanda, where Kabila had waited while Mobutu boarded the ship at Congo's port of Pointe Noire, told Reuters that Mbeki "has gone back to the boat to explain that Kabila is not coming tonight".
The source had few details. "Kabila is not happy with the arrangements. I can't go into what that is," the source added.

Mandela and Mobutu boarded the Russian-built Outeniqua in Pointe Noire earlier -- Mobutu, who has cancer, with great difficulty. Unable to climb 31 steep steps, Mobutu was driven on board five hours late up a make-shift ramp.

The ship then left the port for international waters and a planned rendezvous off Angola with Kabila, whose forces pressed on towards the capital Kinshasa regardless and said they were airlifting men and equipment to the war front.
